key_insight: GRIN+ is a machine unlearning method that removes sensitive training data faster while preserving important medical knowledge, especially in imbalanced datasets.
clinical_relevance: It could help healthcare teams better meet privacy requirements like GDPR/HIPAA without damaging model performance on rare but clinically important conditions.
method: Analyzes gradient contributions from forget and retain sets at the parameter level
Uses class-adaptive influence scoring to reduce majority-class dominance
Applies direction-constrained updates to avoid erasing useful clinical features
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmarking on multiple medical datasets, including ISIC skin cancer, brain tumor MRI, and BUSI breast ultrasound, with improved privacy-utility balance and faster runtime than baselines.
watch_item: Performance may depend on dataset imbalance patterns and careful implementation to ensure the model truly forgets the requested data without harming rare-class accuracy.
paper_title: GRIN+: Towards Fast Yet Effective Machine Unlearning for Imbalanced Medical Data
